classification.difficultyReason: Expand the nested binomial in two stages, identify which inner powers can contribute x^k, and compare their sum with the coefficient in (2+x)^n.

content.prompt:
By considering $(1+(1+x))^n=(2+x)^n$, show that
$$\binom nk\binom kk+\binom n{k+1}\binom{k+1}k+\cdots+\binom nn\binom nk$$
is equal to $\binom nk2^{n-k}$.

answer.short:
$\displaystyle \binom nk\binom kk+\binom n{k+1}\binom{k+1}k+\cdots+\binom nn\binom nk=\binom nk2^{n-k}$.

Expand the nested binomial and equate coefficients of $x^k$.
answer.worked:
Expand the left-hand side using the binomial theorem:
$$\begin{align*}(1+(1+x))^n&=\binom n0+\binom n1(1+x)+\binom n2(1+x)^2+\cdots+\binom nn(1+x)^n.
\end{align*}$$
For $r<k$, $(1+x)^r$ has no $x^k$ term. For $r\geq k$, the coefficient of $x^k$ in $\binom nr(1+x)^r$ is $\binom nr\binom rk$. Thus the coefficient of $x^k$ on the left is
$$\binom nk\binom kk+\binom n{k+1}\binom{k+1}k+\cdots+\binom nn\binom nk.$$
On the right,
$$\begin{align*}(2+x)^n&=\binom n0 2^n+\binom n1 2^{n-1}x+\cdots+\binom nk2^{n-k}x^k+\cdots+x^n.
\end{align*}$$
Its coefficient of $x^k$ is $\binom nk2^{n-k}$. Equating coefficients gives
$$\begin{align*}\binom nk\binom kk+\binom n{k+1}\binom{k+1}k+\cdots+\binom nn\binom nk&=\binom nk2^{n-k}.
\end{align*}$$
